fold_discipline.consequence: A policy selected on a scope that is in-sample for part of the pool is selected on a mixture the sweep cannot claim; the clean pool's own run is data/evidence/combined_clean/report.json.  Re-running the offending members with --fold 0 --eval-fold 1 is queued in SUGGESTIONS.md.

scopes_explained.proxy_dti_selection: DTI on the blocks of fold 0 - the ONLY key that selects. IN-SAMPLE for 3 of 5 members (deep11, nff43, nff45): their training geography includes fold 0. See selection.fold_discipline.
scopes_explained.proxy_dti_measurement: DTI on the blocks of fold 1 - the number to quote, never a selection key. IN-SAMPLE for 3 of 5 members (deep11, nff43, nff45): their training geography includes fold 1. See selection.fold_discipline.
scopes_explained.proxy_dti_pooled01: DTI on the pooled disjoint blocks of folds 0+1. IN-SAMPLE for 3 of 5 members (deep11, nff43, nff45): their training geography includes folds 0, 1. See selection.fold_discipline. Fold 0 is also a selection fold, so the pooled number is not pristine even for a member that held both folds out.
scopes_explained.proxy_dti_whole: whole-grid DTI - REPORTED, NEVER USED TO SELECT: it mixes folds the members held out with folds they trained on, for every member that has a fold protocol at all, so it cannot select anything.

caveats: OUT-OF-SAMPLE STATUS IS PER MEMBER, not per union: the deep-ensemble member was trained over the whole grid (so its contribution to a held-out fold is NOT out-of-sample), while each NFF member holds out its own folds - recorded per member under 'members' above, read from that member's own report.json.  A fold on which a member is in-sample is disclosed here rather than described as held out.

The union is therefore an ensemble of differently-biased detectors, not a set of independent out-of-sample measurements; the only per-member out-of-sample numbers in this repository are the ones in each member's own report.
The proxy population is a stand-in for the private expert labels, not the scored set.  The public leaderboard is the only unbiased test of the transfer.
The catalogue DTI is reported for context only - rules SS1.1/SS3.2 score the new faults in both prize phases.
